Order
This is first application filed by the applicants under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.42/2024, dated 24.03.2024 registered at Police Station-Killod,
District-Khandwa (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n),
376- D of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Applicants are in detention since 11.04.2024. 2 .

As per the prosecution story, on 24.03.2024,
prosecutrix's father lodged an FIR about missing of her 15 years & 9 months old daughter since intervening night of 22-23.03.2024.
He also expressed the suspicion that she might have been taken by Sateesh (applicant).
FIR was registered.

In the 2 MCRC-25370-2024 course of investigation,
prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. stated that on 22.03.2024, Biraj of the village told her that her photograph is with one Bhura Khan and if, she wanted to get the same deleted, she has to reach phatak at 12:00 o'clock of night, therefore, without informing anyone in the home, she went near phatak where Biraj met her and took her on the road where Sateesh alongwith bike was standing.
Thereafter, Biraj put a hankerchief on her mouth, due to which, she became unconscious.
Sateesh and Biraj took her at some unknown place.
When, she woke up, she found herself lying in a hat.
Almost after one hour, Sateesh and Biraj came and gave some food to eat and after having the food (meal), she again became unconscious.
They had continuously committed rape upon her.
On 08.04.2024, in the morning, she woke up and found that one old woman was sleeping and Biraj & Sateesh were not there, therefore, she fled away from there and made a call to her father.
After sometime, her parents reached there and took her back.

After investigation,

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants have submitted that applicants are in detention since 11.04.2024.
They have not committed any offence.
They are innocent.
They have been falsely implicated.

It is a case of false implication and misuse of the provisions of POSCO Act, 2012 as DNA report has been received and from the DNA report, it is apparent that source found on the person of minor girl was neither of Sateesh nor of Biraj.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.

Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail,
pending the trial.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the respondent No.2/victim have opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicants.

But,
learned counsel for the State has fairly admitted that DNA report is negative and Y-chromosome found from the source of the prosecutrix is not of the accused persons.
5 Having taken into consideration the submissions put-forth by learned counsel for the applicants and the DNA report, prima-facie , case appears to be suspicious.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case including the fact that final conclusion of trial of the case will take considerable time, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicants is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicants stands allowed.

6 . It is directed that applicants - Biraj and Sateesh be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for their regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that they shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3)
of Cr.P.C. 7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.

In this case, prosecutrix has already been examined before the Trial Court and she has deposed that she was taken by one boy whose name is not known to her and on basis of telling of boy, she had implicated Biraj and Sateesh (present applicants).

Therefore, police is directed to look into the matter and to make an attempt to nap the real culprit(s) and also to investigate at whose behest these two persons viz. Biraj & Sateesh have been implicated.

.
